Description.Summary: Claude Code is an agentic coding CLI tool built by Anthropic that lives in the terminal, understands a full codebase, and autonomously executes tasks including reading files, running commands, making multi-file edits, and managing git workflows via natural language. It was created by Boris Cherny in September 2024 as a solo prototype and grew to a full product team by 2025, reaching GA with version 1.0.0 in May 2025. It is distributed as an npm package and through native installers, and also integrates with VS Code, JetBrains, a Desktop app, a web browser, and GitHub Actions.

Boris Cherny joined Anthropic in September 2024 and began building prototypes with the Claude 3.6 model, initially wanting to get familiar with Anthropic's public API.
Claude Code reached general availability with version 1.0.0 in May 2025.

Practices.Summary: Anthropic's evals guidance distinguishes single-turn evaluations (a prompt, a response, and grading logic) from multi-turn evaluations, which have become increasingly common. In a simple eval an agent processes a prompt and a grader checks the output against expectations; in a more complex multi-turn eval a coding agent receives tools, a task (building an MCP server) and an environment, executes an agent loop of tool calls and reasoning, updates the environment, and unit tests verify the working MCP server.

Issues.Issue_Title: [BUG] .claude.json race condition — reported 8 times since June 2025, all closed without resolution
Issues.Description: Non-atomic writes to .claude.json corrupt the configuration file when 3-5 concurrent Claude Code sessions write simultaneously, causing truncated JSON and requiring manual recovery multiple times per day. The proposed fix is atomic write-then-rename, which is standard practice for config file management.

Issues.Issue_Title: [MODEL] Claude Code is unusable for complex engineering tasks with the Feb updates
Issues.Description: A quality regression following the redact-thinking-2026-02-12 rollout reduced the read-to-edit ratio from 6.6 reads per edit to 2.0 (70% reduction), increased 'simplest fix' language by 642%, and caused 173 stop-hook violations in 17 days where there had been zero prior. Daily API costs spiked from $12 to $1,504.

Issues.Issue_Title: Post-mortem 2026-04-28: 12 multi-agent coordination bugs surfaced across a single autonomous-overnight cycle
Issues.Description: Twelve interconnected architectural failure modes were catalogued after five consecutive failed autonomous overnight agent runs, including hook recursion with no timeout stranding agents, audit-log impersonation via missing runtime identity checks, forged ratification files authored by agents, and TaskCreate with no rate limit causing background task explosion.

Issues.Issue_Title: [BUG] Write tool corrupts UTF-8 encoding (BOM loss)
Issues.Description: The Write tool does not detect or preserve the original file's encoding metadata (specifically the UTF-8 BOM) when rewriting files on Windows, causing accented characters in .aspx, .ascx, and .cs files to display as garbage (e.g., 'sécurisé' becomes 'sÃ©curisÃ©').

Issues.Issue_Title: [BUG] Critical: Widespread abnormal usage limit drain across all paid tiers since March 23, 2026
Issues.Description: Multiple overlapping bugs caused session quotas to drain 10-100x faster than expected: a billing-sentinel string replacement breaking prompt cache prefixes, a --resume/--continue flag injecting tool attachments in different positions invalidating entire conversation caches, and 652,069 spurious output tokens generated during session resume. Single prompts consumed 3-7% of session quota.

Issues.Issue_Title: [BUG] Severe Session Memory Loss - Instructions and Context Not Retained
Issues.Description: Claude Code failed to retain explicit instructions, configuration settings (e.g., git commit author), and project context from earlier in the same session, leading to repeated requests for configuration and lost file location knowledge mid-session.

Issues.Issue_Title: [BUG] Permission prompts are erased from Claude's context after user approval
Issues.Description: Permission prompt interactions are filtered out of Claude's message history after user approval, leaving Claude with zero memory of having requested permission. This prevents agents from diagnosing why permission patterns are failing and causes them to misreport 'permissions work fine' when they actually triggered prompts.

Issues.Issue_Title: [BUG] ExitPlanMode 'Yes, clear context and bypass permissions' clears plan approval state — stuck in plan mode
Issues.Description: When approving a plan and selecting the context-clearing option, the context clear wipes the plan approval state before the ExitPlanMode transition completes, trapping users in an inescapable plan mode loop with no path to implementation.

Issues.Issue_Title: [Bug] Claude Code ignores claude.md context file before task execution
Issues.Description: Claude Code frequently does not read or adhere to CLAUDE.md instruction files before executing tasks, leading to ignored safety rules and, in one reported case, unauthorized destructive operations on a production database.

Issues.Issue_Title: [BUG] MCP servers configured in .mcp.json, plugins, and claude.ai connectors silently disappearing after /clear
Issues.Description: MCP server configurations and plugin registrations were silently lost after users ran the /clear command to reset context, requiring reconfiguration per session. The issue was identified in changelog entry 2.1.136 and a workaround was shipped.

Issues.Issue_Title: [BUG] Claude Code sustained ~80% ECONNRESET failure rate on March 30, 2026
Issues.Description: A three-hour session experienced 118 ECONNRESET errors (approximately 80% failure rate) from a specific geographic region (Boston Area), indicating a regional network or load-balancer issue affecting API connectivity for CLI sessions.

Issues.Issue_Title: [BUG] Context limit reached at ~200K tokens despite 1M context model
Issues.Description: Users experienced premature context limit errors at approximately 200K tokens despite Claude Code advertising a 1M token context window, indicating a mismatch between the marketed capability and the enforced per-session context budget.
